name: Germany
eu_tuition: €0 tuition at public universities
eu_summary: Public universities in Germany do not charge tuition for Bachelor's, Master's or PhD studies. This applies to German, EU/EEA and (with the exception of Baden-Württemberg) non-EU students as well. Students pay only a semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) covering administration and, in most cases, a public transport ticket.
public_universities: Generally tuition-free; a mandatory semester contribution applies.
private_universities: Private universities charge tuition (frequently €5,000–€25,000 per year). Only a minority are state-recognised and fee-bearing.
bachelor: Tuition-free at public universities; semester contribution applies.
master: Tuition-free at public universities; some continuing-education or part-time Master's formats are fee-based.
phd: Generally tuition-free; doctoral candidates are usually employed or scholarship-funded.
english_taught: A large and growing catalogue of English-taught Master's programmes, and a smaller number of English-taught Bachelor's programmes, especially at technical and private institutions.
mandatory_fees: Semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) of roughly €150–€400 per semester, varying by university; it usually includes a public transport semester ticket and student services.
residency_conditions: No residency requirement for tuition-free status at public universities. Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU/EEA students €1,500 per semester; EU/EEA citizens are exempt from that charge.
language_requirements: German-taught programmes require proof of German (commonly DSH-2/TestDaF). English-taught programmes require English proof (IELTS/TOEFL), level set by each programme.
application_system: uni-assist e.V. (for many universities) and direct university portals; DoSV/hochschulstart for some medicine/restricted programmes.

sources.label: DAAD / Studying in Germany – costs and fees
EU Education portal – Country profile: Germany

document_submission.documents: Certified copies of certificates + transcripts (certified German/English translation); original documents checked at enrolment.
document_submission.note: Via uni-assist for participating universities — submit 4–6 weeks before the deadline.

housing: Student dormitories (Studentenwohnheime) are the cheapest option but heavily oversubscribed — apply as soon as you are admitted; shared flats (WG) are common.
scholarships: Tuition-free study means funding usually targets living costs; see DAAD scholarships and university awards.

name: Austria
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for regular study duration; conditional fee afterwards
eu_summary: EU/EEA (and Swiss) citizens pay no tuition at public universities as long as they study within the minimum duration plus two semesters. Beyond that, a fee of €363.36 per semester applies. All students pay the mandatory ÖH students' union fee.
public_universities: Tuition-free for EU/EEA within regular duration; ÖH fee always payable.
private_universities: Private universities charge tuition (often €2,000–€25,000 per year).
bachelor: €0 tuition for EU/EEA within regular duration; ÖH fee applies.
master: €0 tuition for EU/EEA within regular duration; ÖH fee applies.
phd: €0 tuition for EU/EEA within regular duration; ÖH fee applies.
english_taught: Many English-taught Master's programmes; fewer English-taught Bachelor's programmes (more common at private universities).
mandatory_fees: ÖH students' union fee of approximately €24.70 per semester (indexed annually). A conditional tuition fee of €363.36 per semester applies to EU/EEA students exceeding minimum duration + 2 semesters.
residency_conditions: No residency requirement. Non-EU/EEA students pay €726.72 per semester from the first semester, unless covered by an exemption.
language_requirements: German-taught programmes require German (commonly level C1 or a recognised diploma). English-taught programmes set their own English requirements.
application_system: Direct university portals; many institutions support the joint Austrian application system for some programmes.

sources.label: University of Vienna – Amount of the tuition fee / Students' Union fee
EU Education portal – Country profile: Austria

document_submission.documents: Certified copies + translations; originals checked at enrolment.
document_submission.note: Apply directly to the university; allow time for document certification.

housing: Student halls (Studentenheime) and shared flats; the OeAD provides housing services.
scholarships: See OeAD grants and university scholarships; the ÖH advises students.

name: Finland
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for EU/EEA and Swiss citizens
eu_summary: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens are not liable for tuition fees at Finnish universities and universities of applied sciences, including English-taught degree programmes. Non-EU/EEA students (with exceptions) pay fees of roughly €8,000–€20,000 per year. Doctoral studies remain free of charge.
public_universities: Tuition-free for EU/EEA; a compulsory student union / student services fee applies.
private_universities: Finland's higher education sector is publicly funded; only a few private institutions operate, mainly in business and design.
bachelor: €0 tuition for EU/EEA; student union fee applies.
master: €0 tuition for EU/EEA; student union fee applies.
phd: Free of charge for all students.
english_taught: One of Europe's largest English-taught catalogues at Bachelor's and Master's level.
mandatory_fees: Compulsory student union fee of roughly €60–€120 per year (varies between universities; includes student health care), plus a small one-off registration/administrative fee at some institutions.
residency_conditions: Citizenship-based: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens are exempt. From 2025, applicants from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland pay a €100 application fee for Bachelor's programmes.
language_requirements: English-taught programmes require English proof (commonly IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 92, set per programme); Finnish/Swedish-taught programmes require national language proof.
application_system: Studyinfo (opintopolku.fi) national joint application; some Master's admissions are direct.

sources.label: Studyinfo – Tuition fees
Metropolia UAS – Tuition fees for non-EU/EEA students

document_submission.documents: Upload certificates to the Studyinfo application; certified copies may be requested later.
document_submission.note: Some Master’s programmes have separate, later rounds.

housing: Student housing foundations (e.g. HOAS in Helsinki) offer affordable rooms — apply early.
scholarships: Many English-taught programmes offer merit scholarships; EU/EEA students pay no tuition.

name: Sweden
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for EU/EEA and Swiss citizens
eu_summary: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens do not pay application or tuition fees at Swedish universities for Bachelor's or Master's studies. Non-EU/EEA students pay tuition (average around SEK 129,000 per year).
public_universities: Tuition-free for EU/EEA; a small mandatory student union fee at some institutions.
private_universities: A few private institutions exist (e.g. in business or design) and may charge fees.
master: €0 tuition for EU/EEA.
phd: Doctoral education is normally free and often salaried.
english_taught: Very large English-taught catalogue, especially at Master's level.
mandatory_fees: Most universities charge a small student union fee (roughly SEK 50–350 per semester); no tuition and no application fee for EU/EEA applicants.
residency_conditions: Citizenship-based exemption for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens.
language_requirements: English-taught programmes require English proof (commonly English 6 / IELTS 6.5); Swedish-taught programmes require Swedish proof.
application_system: universityadmissions.se (national joint application).

sources.label: University Admissions Sweden – Who is required to pay fees?
Study in Sweden – Information for EU citizens

document_submission.documents: Upload documents to universityadmissions.se; certified copies/translations for some.
document_submission.note: National joint application; late applications only if places remain.

housing: Housing via universities/student unions and nations; queues can be long in Uppsala, Lund and Stockholm.
scholarships: Swedish Institute scholarships target international students; EU/EEA pay no tuition.

name: Denmark
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for EU/EEA and Swiss citizens
eu_summary: Higher education at Danish public universities is free for students from the EU/EEA and Switzerland, at Bachelor's and Master's level. Non-EU/EEA students pay tuition of roughly €6,000–€16,000 per year.
public_universities: Tuition-free for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens.
private_universities: A small number of private institutions charge tuition.
master: €0 tuition for EU/EEA.
phd: Doctoral positions are salaried and free of tuition.
english_taught: Large English-taught catalogue, especially at Master's level.
mandatory_fees: No tuition; some institutions apply small administrative or student organisation fees.
residency_conditions: Citizenship-based exemption for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens.
language_requirements: English-taught programmes require English proof (commonly IELTS 6.5); Danish-taught programmes require Danish proof.
application_system: Direct university portals; optagelse.dk for some Bachelor's programmes.

sources.label: Study in Denmark – Tuition Fees

document_submission.documents: Certified copies + translations; submit via optagelse.dk or the institution.

housing: Student housing via municipalities and student organisations; apply early, especially in Copenhagen.
scholarships: Danish government and university scholarships exist; EU/EEA pay no tuition.

name: Norway
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for EU/EEA and Swiss citizens
eu_summary: Norway is not an EU member but is in the EEA. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens study without tuition fees at Norwegian public universities. From autumn 2023, students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland are charged tuition (commonly NOK 60,000–NOK 85,000+ per year, set by each institution).
public_universities: Tuition-free for EU/EEA; a small semester fee applies.
master: €0 tuition for EU/EEA.
phd: Doctoral education is free and normally salaried.
english_taught: Broad English-taught catalogue at Master's level; fewer English-taught Bachelor's programmes.
mandatory_fees: Semester fee (semesteravgift) of roughly NOK 500–NOK 800 per semester, covering the student welfare organisation and student union.
residency_conditions: Citizenship-based exemption for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens; non-EEA students pay tuition from 2023.
language_requirements: English-taught programmes require English proof; Norwegian-taught programmes require Norwegian proof.
application_system: Direct university portals; some joint national arrangements.

sources.label: NTNU – Tuition fees for Master's degrees in English
Study in Norway – Cost and requirements

document_submission.documents: Certified copies + translations; documentation of financing (non-EEA).

housing: Student welfare organisations (SiO/Sit) provide housing — apply early.
scholarships: Lånekassen (state loan fund) supports students; some university scholarships exist.

name: Iceland
eu_tuition: €0 tuition at public universities (registration fee only)
eu_summary: Iceland is not an EU member but is in the EEA. Public universities in Iceland do not charge tuition fees; students pay only an annual registration/administration fee. This applies broadly to all students at public institutions.
public_universities: No tuition; annual registration fee only.
private_universities: Some private institutions charge fees, though a few remain low-cost.
bachelor: No tuition at public universities; registration fee applies.
master: No tuition at public universities; registration fee applies.
phd: Doctoral studies at public universities generally carry no tuition fee.
english_taught: A moderate and growing English-taught catalogue at Master's level; some Bachelor's programmes in English.
mandatory_fees: Annual registration fee, for example around ISK 75,000 (≈ €500) at some institutions; the University of Iceland lists a lower annual registration fee — verify per institution.
residency_conditions: Applies broadly; verify per institution.
language_requirements: English-taught programmes require English proof; Icelandic-taught programmes require Icelandic proof.
application_system: Direct university portals.

sources.label: University of Iceland – University fees
Study in Iceland – Universities

document_submission.documents: Certified copies + translations, submitted directly.

housing: Very limited market in the Reykjavík area; apply early through student services.
scholarships: Icelandic state student loan fund (LÍN); limited scholarships.

name: Greece
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for Greek-taught undergraduate programmes
eu_summary: Public universities in Greece do not charge tuition for Greek-taught undergraduate (first-cycle) programmes, for EU/EEA and Swiss students as well as for others, subject to admission. Some postgraduate and English-taught programmes charge fees.
public_universities: Tuition-free at undergraduate level; postgraduate fees vary.
private_universities: Greece's higher-education sector is almost entirely public; private provision has been expanding under recent reforms.
master: Fees vary; some programmes are free, others charge tuition.
phd: Often free or low-cost; verify per institution.
english_taught: A growing number of English-taught Master's programmes, some with fees.
mandatory_fees: No standard tuition; small administrative costs may apply. Verify per institution.
residency_conditions: No tuition for undergraduate programmes; admission for EU/EEA applicants follows national recognition rules.
language_requirements: Greek-taught programmes require Greek; English-taught programmes require English proof.
application_system: National admission via the Ministry / platform; international applicants apply directly to institutions.

sources.label: EU Education portal – Country profile: Greece

document_submission.documents: Recognition/equivalence of foreign certificates; certified copies + official translations.
document_submission.note: Undergraduate international admission follows national procedures — verify.

housing: Shared flats dominate; university housing is limited.
scholarships: IKY (State Scholarships Foundation) offers scholarships.

name: Czechia
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for programmes taught in Czech
eu_summary: Study at public universities is free of charge for all students, including international students, when the programme is taught in Czech and studied within standard duration. Programmes taught in English (and other foreign languages) are subject to tuition fees.
public_universities: Free in the Czech language; English-taught programmes are fee-based.
master: €0 in Czech; fees in English.
phd: Often free and sometimes salaried; some English-taught doctoral programmes are fee-based.
english_taught: Over 1,000 programmes in English; these generally carry tuition fees.
mandatory_fees: No tuition for Czech-taught programmes; small administrative/application fees may apply.
residency_conditions: Condition is language of instruction and standard duration, not nationality.
language_requirements: Czech-taught programmes require Czech (often B2 or a preparatory year); English programmes require English proof.
application_system: Direct university portals; many offer a one-year Czech-language preparatory programme.

sources.label: Study in Czechia (official portal)
Charles University – Study with us

document_submission.documents: Certificate + recognition of foreign secondary education (nostrification) where required.

housing: Dormitories (koleje) are affordable; Prague is competitive.
scholarships: Government scholarships for Czech-language study; university merit scholarships.

name: Poland
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for Polish-taught programmes for EU citizens
eu_summary: EU/EEA citizens may study free of charge at Polish public universities when the programme is taught in Polish (subject to the same rules as Polish citizens). Programmes taught in English and other foreign languages are generally fee-based.
public_universities: Free in Polish for EU/EEA; fee-based in English.
bachelor: €0 in Polish for EU/EEA; fee-based in English.
master: €0 in Polish for EU/EEA; fee-based in English.
phd: Free or low-cost in Polish; fee-based in English (some doctoral schools are free for all).
english_taught: Large and growing English-taught catalogue (1,000+ programmes), mostly fee-based.
mandatory_fees: No tuition for Polish-taught study; small administrative fees may apply.
residency_conditions: EU/EEA citizens study on the same terms as Polish citizens in Polish-taught programmes.
language_requirements: Polish-taught programmes require Polish (often B1/B2 or a preparatory year); English programmes require English proof.
application_system: Direct university portals; national systems such as IRK per university.

sources.label: Study in Poland (official)
EU Education portal – Country profile: Poland

document_submission.documents: Legalisation/apostille + sworn translation often required.

housing: Dormitories (akademiki) are cheap; private rentals widely available.
scholarships: NAWA scholarships (e.g. Banach) and university merit scholarships.

name: Slovenia
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for full-time study for EU citizens
eu_summary: At Slovenian public universities, full-time Bachelor's and Master's studies are free of tuition for Slovenian citizens and EU/EEA citizens (generally also for other eligible categories). Part-time and some English-taught programmes may be fee-based.
public_universities: Tuition-free for full-time study for eligible students; small enrolment fee may apply.
master: €0 for full-time study (eligible students).
phd: Often free or low-cost; verify per institution.
english_taught: A moderate English-taught catalogue; some English programmes are fee-based.
mandatory_fees: Small enrolment/administration fee may apply for candidates who have already completed the same level of education.
residency_conditions: EU/EEA citizens are treated on the same basis as Slovenian citizens for full-time study.
language_requirements: Slovene-taught programmes require Slovene; English programmes require English proof.
application_system: National application portal (eVŠ) for entry to study, plus direct institution portals.

sources.label: University of Ljubljana – Tuition fees and other contributions
Study in Slovenia – Tuition and Funding

document_submission.closes: Spring round ≈ March; later rounds in summer
document_submission.documents: Certified copies + translations; originals at enrolment.
document_submission.note: Enrolment via the national eVŠ portal.

housing: Subsidised student dormitories (študentski domovi) — apply early, especially in Ljubljana.
scholarships: Slovenian government scholarships (bilateral) and university support.

name: Estonia
eu_tuition: €0 in Estonian-language study places; fee-based in English
eu_summary: In Estonia, EU/EEA citizens can study free of charge in Estonian-taught programmes when admitted to a state-commissioned (free) study place. English-taught programmes generally charge tuition for all students, including EU/EEA citizens, in the range of roughly €1,660–€7,500 per year.
public_universities: Free in Estonian study places; English programmes are typically fee-based.
bachelor: €0 in Estonian study places; fees in English.
master: €0 in Estonian study places; fees in English.
phd: Doctoral study is often free and salaried.
english_taught: A strong English-taught catalogue at Master's level, mostly fee-based; some scholarships available.
mandatory_fees: No tuition in Estonian study places; small administrative fees may apply.
residency_conditions: Condition is language of instruction and study-place type, not nationality.
language_requirements: Estonian-taught programmes require Estonian (often B2); English programmes require English proof.
application_system: National admission via SAIS (sais.ee) and direct institution portals.

sources.label: Study in Estonia – Master's programmes

document_submission.documents: Certified copies + translations, submitted via SAIS or directly.

housing: Dormitories available; Tallinn and Tartu markets are competitive.
scholarships: Estonian government and university scholarships; some programmes offer tuition waivers.

name: France
eu_tuition: National rate: €178/year Bachelor's, €254/year Master's
eu_summary: France charges low national tuition rates at public universities. For 2025-2026 these were €178 per year for a Licence (Bachelor's) and €254 per year for a Master's. Non-EU students from outside the EU/EEA may be charged differentiated (higher) rates unless exempted. Doctoral tuition is very low.
public_universities: Low national tuition rates for EU/EEA students.
private_universities: Private and some grande école programmes charge higher fees.
master: ≈ €254 per year (national rate).
phd: ≈ €391 per year (national rate).
english_taught: Growing English-taught catalogue, especially at Master's level.
mandatory_fees: Additional contributions such as the CVEC campus contribution (around €100–€175 per year) may apply.
residency_conditions: Differentiated fees may apply to non-EU/EEA students; EU/EEA citizens pay the national rate.
language_requirements: French-taught programmes require French (commonly B2 via DELF/DALF/TCF); English programmes require English proof.
application_system: Parcoursup (Bachelor's) and Mon Master / Études en France for international applicants.

sources.label: EU Education portal – Country profile: France
Service-Public – University fees

document_submission.closes: Parcoursup ≈ March–April; Mon Master ≈ March; Études en France earlier (Nov–Mar)
document_submission.documents: Certified translations may be required; Études en France for many international applicants.
document_submission.note: Bachelor’s via Parcoursup; Master’s via Mon Master.

housing: CROUS student residences are cheap but oversubscribed; private rentals are common.
scholarships: Eiffel Excellence and Campus France scholarships; low national tuition for EU/EEA.

name: Netherlands
eu_tuition: Statutory fee ≈ €2,694 for 2026-2027 (EU/EEA)
eu_summary: EU/EEA students pay the government-set statutory tuition fee at Dutch public universities: €2,694 for the 2026-2027 academic year for full-time study. Non-EU/EEA students pay the higher institutional fee.
public_universities: Statutory fee applies for EU/EEA.
private_universities: Private institutions set their own fees.
master: Statutory fee applies (some programmes are institutional-fee only).
phd: PhD candidates are usually employed and pay no tuition.
english_taught: Very large English-taught catalogue at Bachelor's and Master's level.
mandatory_fees: No separate mandatory semester fee beyond the statutory tuition fee; some institutions add small administrative costs.
residency_conditions: Statutory fee depends on nationality/residency conditions (EU/EEA/Swiss or qualifying residence permit).
language_requirements: English-taught programmes require English proof; Dutch-taught programmes require Dutch proof.
application_system: Direct university portals and Studielink (national enrolment).

sources.label: Study in NL – Tuition fees

document_submission.documents: Certified copies + translations; register via Studielink, then upload to the institution.
document_submission.note: Selection procedures may add earlier deadlines.

housing: Housing is scarce — start very early; student housing corporations plus the private market.
scholarships: Holland Scholarship and university awards for non-EU; EU/EEA pay the statutory fee.

name: Ireland
eu_tuition: €0 tuition under Free Fees Initiative; student contribution ≈ €2,500–€3,000/year
eu_summary: Eligible EU/EEA students in Ireland do not pay tuition under the Free Fees Initiative, but must pay a student contribution charge (€2,500 for 2025/26). Eligibility requires qualifying residency conditions (for example, time spent in EU/EEA/UK education).
public_universities: Tuition covered by Free Fees Initiative; student contribution payable.
bachelor: Tuition-free if eligible; student contribution payable.
master: Free Fees generally applies to undergraduate; postgraduate fees vary.
phd: Postgraduate fees vary; some funding available.
english_taught: Predominantly English-taught; a large catalogue for international students.
mandatory_fees: Student contribution charge of €2,500 for 2025/26 (may rise), payable by eligible students.
residency_conditions: Free Fees eligibility depends on EU/EEA/UK nationality plus residency/education history criteria.
language_requirements: English-taught; require English proof for non-native speakers.
application_system: CAO (Central Applications Office) for undergraduate; direct for postgraduate.

Citizens Information – Third-level student fees and charges

document_submission.documents: Certified copies + translations; submit via CAO (undergraduate) or directly (postgraduate).

housing: On-campus and private student accommodation; Dublin is expensive — book early.
scholarships: Government of Ireland scholarships and university awards.

name: Hungary
eu_tuition: €0 in state-funded (scholarship) places; fee-based in self-financed places
eu_summary: Hungarian public universities offer a number of state-funded (tuition-free) study places, awarded on merit, which EU/EEA citizens may take up on the same basis as Hungarian citizens. Other students study in self-financed, fee-paying places. The Stipendium Hungaricum programme provides additional fully funded scholarships.
public_universities: Free in state-funded places; fees in self-financed places.
bachelor: Free if admitted to a state-funded place.
master: Free if admitted to a state-funded place.
phd: Doctoral schools often include state scholarships.
english_taught: A large English-taught catalogue, frequently fee-based.
mandatory_fees: No tuition in state-funded places; small administrative costs may apply.
residency_conditions: State-funded places are merit-based and open to EU/EEA applicants on equal terms.
language_requirements: Hungarian-taught programmes require Hungarian; English programmes require English proof.
application_system: Direct institution portals; Stipendium Hungaricum via the national scholarship system.

document_submission.documents: Certified copies + official translations; entrance exam where required.

housing: Dormitories and private rentals; Budapest is competitive.
scholarships: Stipendium Hungaricum (fully funded) and state-funded (tuition-free) places.

name: Belgium
eu_tuition: Low tuition: Flemish Community ≈ €1,181, Wallonia-Brussels Federation max €1,194 (EU/EEA, 2026-2027)
eu_summary: Belgian public universities charge relatively low tuition, set separately by the Flemish Community and the Wallonia-Brussels Federation. For 2026-2027 the Flemish rate for a full-time EU/EEA degree programme is about €1,181.40 per year. In the Wallonia-Brussels Federation, EU nationals pay a maximum of about €1,194 per year, with reduced categories paying roughly €175–€835.
public_universities: Low tuition for EU/EEA; the exact amount depends on the Community (Flanders or Wallonia-Brussels) and the institution.
private_universities: A limited private sector charges higher fees.
bachelor: Low tuition (EU/EEA rate) — see the relevant Community rate.
master: Low tuition (EU/EEA rate); some advanced Master’s may differ.
phd: Doctoral candidates are usually salaried or funded.
english_taught: Growing English-taught catalogue, especially at Master’s level.
mandatory_fees: No large separate mandatory semester fee; small administrative charges may apply.
residency_conditions: EU/EEA students are charged the standard (lower) rate; non-EU/EEA rates are higher and vary by programme.
language_requirements: Programmes are taught in Dutch, French or English; language proof required accordingly.
application_system: Direct institution portals; some programmes use joint enrolment procedures.

scholarships: University scholarships and community grants.

name: Bulgaria
eu_tuition: Low tuition — all students (incl. EU/EEA) pay tuition at public universities
eu_summary: In Bulgaria, all students are required to pay tuition fees in the first and second cycle — there is no general tuition-free route for EU citizens. Fees are set by the institutions and are relatively low compared with Western Europe; EU/EEA students generally pay the same rates as Bulgarian students.
public_universities: Tuition is charged to all students; amounts are set by each institution and are comparatively low.
private_universities: Private institutions charge tuition, typically higher than public ones.
bachelor: Tuition charged (low by European standards); amount varies by institution and field.
master: Tuition charged; amount varies by institution and field.
phd: Doctoral study is often funded or low-cost — verify per institution.
english_taught: A moderate English-taught catalogue, frequently fee-based.
mandatory_fees: No separate mandatory semester fee; tuition is the main charge. Small administrative fees may apply.
residency_conditions: EU/EEA students generally pay the same tuition as Bulgarian students.
language_requirements: Bulgarian-taught programmes require Bulgarian; English programmes require English proof.
application_system: Direct institution portals; some programmes via the Ministry’s admission rules.

scholarships: Government scholarships for Bulgarian-language study; low fees.

name: Croatia
eu_tuition: €0 tuition for Croatian-taught degrees at public universities (full-time)
eu_summary: At Croatian public universities, degrees taught in Croatian generally do not charge tuition fees, and full-time EU/EEA students are treated on the same basis as Croatian citizens. Programmes taught in foreign languages (e.g. English) and some part-time or quota-exceeding enrolments may be fee-based.
public_universities: Croatian-taught degrees generally tuition-free; foreign-language programmes may be fee-based.
bachelor: €0 for Croatian-taught full-time study; foreign-language programmes may charge fees.
master: €0 for Croatian-taught full-time study; foreign-language programmes may charge fees.
phd: Often low-cost or funded — verify per institution.
english_taught: A moderate English-taught catalogue, frequently fee-based.
mandatory_fees: Small enrolment/administrative fees may apply (application fee roughly €60–€300 in some cases).
residency_conditions: EU/EEA students are treated on the same basis as Croatian citizens for Croatian-taught study.
language_requirements: Croatian-taught programmes require Croatian; English programmes require English proof.
application_system: National portal (postani-student.hr) and direct institution portals.

EU Education portal – Country profile: Croatia

housing: Subsidised student dormitories (studentski dom); Zagreb is competitive.
scholarships: Government (bilateral) scholarships and university support.

name: Cyprus
eu_tuition: First-cycle may be tuition-free for EU students at public universities — sources conflict; verify
eu_summary: The situation for EU students in Cyprus is contradictory across official sources. The European Commission’s country profile states that EU students do not pay tuition fees for first-cycle programmes at public universities, with the exception of the Open University of Cyprus.
